Theme

School & learning

volume noun

one book of a set or a long work

also volumes, tome, vol.

classical

Cic. Tusc. 3.6: hoc tertium volūmen
Nep. Att. 16.3: sēdecim volūmina epistulārum (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. volume (book)

volūmen, volūminis n.

noun, third declension

a volume; properly a roll

From volvō: a roll of writing, and so one book of a longer work. In poetry and post-Augustan prose also a coil or fold (of a snake, Verg. A. 2.208) or a wreath of smoke. Not the volume of sound (see volume, loudness).

Other words

  • liber, librī m. — a book; one book of a work

    noun, second declension · also used · classical

    The plain word for a book, and the usual way to number the parts of a work: liber tertius.

  • tomus, tomī m. — a volume, a tome

    noun, second declension · also used · post-classical · M. Aurel. ap. Fronto: in quīnque tomīs (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. volume (book)

    Greek τόμος, a piece cut off; in Martial (1.67.3, Lewis & Short) a cheap roll of paper, in Marcus Aurelius one part of a longer work.

Examples

  • sed quoniam duōbus superiōribus dē morte et dē dolōre dictum est, tertius diēs disputātiōnis hoc tertium volūmen efficiet.

    but since death and pain were dealt with in the two earlier ones, the third day of the discussion will make this third volume.Cic. Tusc. 3.6

See also book, volume, library.

SourcesLewis & Short: volumen · Lewis & Short: liber · Lewis & Short: tomus
